bullets.title: APP +24%, U +18%: Both pair-trade legs working simultaneously post-earnings
bullets.body: AppLovin reported 3Q revenues +14% q/q with 4Q guidance of 8-10% sequential growth; Citi reiterates Buy at $500 PT. Unity's Vector unit grew 40% q/q with 4Q guidance of 21-23% sequential growth. Morgan Stanley notes both names surging simultaneously despite historical short positioning between them.

bullets.title: SNAP: Citi cuts PT to $6, keeps Neutral — DR strong but Brand ads drag
bullets.body: Citi lowered PT to $6 (from prior level), maintaining Neutral/High Risk. 3Q DAUs of 495M (+4% Y/Y) missed consensus by ~1% on slower ROW growth; adj. EBITDA margin expanded +10pts Y/Y to 22.2% with 93% incremental flow-through. Direct Response now 77% of revenue (Sponsored Snaps +56% Q/Q), but upper-funnel Brand ads declined Y/Y; management expects Brand rebound in 2027. SNAP fell -11.1% pre-market.

bullets.title: QCOM -12% post-earnings: margin compression from DC ramp costs overshadows DC ambition
bullets.body: Q4 beat on revenue (+3.2%) but gross margin of 50.8% came in 250bps below consensus driven by data-center ramp expenses. Q1 EBT margin guidance of 20-22% was 330bps below FactSet expectations. Management targets $650M+ DC revenue in Q1 and $7B annualized exit FY27, but DC custom silicon is dilutive to gross margins near-term. Sell-side average PT cut 3.8% to $191.10; stock -8.5% post-earnings, -12.2% pre-market.

bullets.title: FWONK +6%: Malone surrenders voting control, F1 revenues +28% Y/Y
bullets.body: F1 revenues grew +28% Y/Y to $1.12B on a 23-race calendar; F1 OIBDA of $338M YTD vs. UBSe $299M. John Malone exchanged ~48% high-vote Series B shares, reducing voting interest to ~3%, which both UBS and Citi view as enhancing strategic flexibility and potentially injecting M&A premium. MotoGP revenues declined 34% Y/Y to $111M, primarily driving the slight 3Q consolidated miss. Citi maintains Buy at $100 PT; UBS maintains Neutral.

bullets.title: CSCO downgraded to Equal-Weight at MS: re-rating played out, AI mix a margin headwind
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley cuts CSCO from Overweight to Equal-Weight, arguing the re-rating thesis has fully played out and lower-margin AI product mix reduces the probability of positive earnings surprises going forward.

bullets.title: DDOG -15%: Citi 'buying the weakness,' cuts PT to $290 from $305
bullets.body: Fatima Boolani argues core SKUs are accelerating with AI-native customers choosing Datadog over DIY solutions, supporting 25%+ topline/FCF/OPM growth. Valuation at 12x EV/Sales '27 and 44x EV/FCF '27. PT trimmed to $290 from $305; Buy maintained.

bullets.title: HUBS: Multiple downgrades, Citi cuts PT to $230 from $287 on guidance slash
bullets.body: HubSpot added only 5,258 net new customers vs. ~10,900 Y/Y, with pronounced downmarket headwinds and longer enterprise sales cycles. Q4 revenue guidance came in $18M below consensus; net-new ARR declining Y/Y. Morgan Stanley also pushes out recovery timeline. Citi TP cut to $230 from $287. HUBS traded -4.4% pre-market.

bullets.title: AMAT: Citi maintains Buy at $710 PT ahead of 11/12 earnings; supply chain constraints a near-term risk to peers
bullets.body: Citi keeps $224B/$286B CY27/28 WFE forecasts and argues AMAT's scale and >2x manufacturing capacity expansion enable better supply-chain management than peers facing MFC, PCB, and DRAM shortages. CY30 targets include 54% non-GAAP GM, >200bps WFE share gains, and advanced packaging revenue exceeding $5B. HBM revenue >$1B in CY26 with >60% share. PT implies 92% upside at 28x 2028E P/E.

bullets.title: MSFT: Management turns negative on neocloud partners; lower Q1 capex tied to IREN delays
bullets.body: Bloomberg reports Microsoft leadership increasingly skeptical of neocloud data-center developers, citing project delays, regulatory headwinds, and rising costs. MSFT increased oversight of partnerships with Iren, Nebius, and Nscale, and declined to expand its Nscale agreement. MSFT's lower-than-expected Q1 capex is attributed to IREN project delays. MSFT +6.7% on the day as a hyperscaler beneficiary of blue-wave permitting dynamics.

bullets.title: AI/datacenter infrastructure basket -10%+: Texas regulatory risk and neocloud delivery uncertainty dominate
bullets.body: Democratic sweep in Texas (home to ~20% of projected 2030 datacenter buildout) sent AI Power basket -10.4%; CEG -6.7%, VST -13.8%, CIFR -20%; IREN -11.8%, CRWV -9%. Post-midterm commentary flags complex multi-party contracts between compute and power offtakers facing delivery-date scrutiny, with buyers likely to shift demand toward states with clearer grid certainty. Wolfe Research argues existing under-construction pipeline will absorb near-term semis demand and state moratoria won't stop projects outright.

bullets.title: Semiconductor sector under severe pressure: SOXX -12% intraday, QQQ near historical lows
bullets.body: GS desk notes QQQ down ~6% (worst day since DeepSeek, in ~15% drawdown) with SOXX down ~12% matching COVID and 2022 tech recession drawdown levels. VIX spiked 45-65%. Long-only flows now 55% of Tech notional vs. HFs 45%, a flip from prior AI reactions. MU suspended its $4.5B Taiwan chip plant on a labor dispute; AMD -6.1%, MU -5.0%, MRVL -4.7%, LITE -4.6%, STX -5.4% all trading lower pre-market.

bullets.title: MRVL/LITE merger: Raymond James sees compelling strategic logic, maintains Strong Buy on both
bullets.body: Raymond James argues the Marvell/Lumentum combination has strong industrial rationale as NPO and CPO become critical for connecting accelerators and switches. Marvell brings DSPs, SerDes, and custom silicon; Lumentum provides lasers, optical components, and photonic manufacturing. Optical margins have improved structurally from industry consolidation. Implications discussed for COHR, NVDA, AVGO, CIEN, CSCO, and NOK.

bullets.title: AMZN-Uber food delivery partnership: DASH -3.2% pre-market, Lyft Go bundle launched
bullets.body: Amazon is partnering with Uber (Dara K's company) for free Prime restaurant delivery, replacing the prior GrubHub/Wonder partnership. DoorDash -3.2% in pre-market reaction. Separately, DASH and LYFT launched a new Lyft Go membership ($9.99) bundled with DashPass, with a lower tier at $4.99.

bullets.title: EXPE: Citi cuts PT to $330 from $345, maintains Neutral; OTA multiples converging
bullets.body: Expedia beat 3Q with Room Nights +7% Y/Y and +2% above consensus, but Q4 guidance came in slightly below on Fall Sale timing shift, elections, and Middle East conflict. Ron Josey lowers PT to $330 from $345, maintaining Neutral, with preference for BKNG as OTA multiples converge. EXPE -7.8% pre-market.

bullets.title: FIG (Figma): AI consumption 2.5x since Oct-6 Agent GA; Citi raises PT to $34
bullets.body: Figma revenue grew +43% Y/Y with NDR above 130%; AI consumption has grown 2.5x since the Agent GA launch on Oct 6, contributing six points of revenue growth. Q4 guidance came in $13M above consensus; operating income beat by $23M. Citi raises TP to $34. FIG was -6.9% pre-market despite the strong print (likely profit-taking after prior run).

bullets.title: TMUS: Citi updates model for $21.5B 2027 spectrum spend; PT $165 Neutral unchanged
bullets.body: Citi trimmed TMUS estimates to reflect higher capitalized interest from potential future spectrum purchases, updated D&A for intangible amortization, and reduced 2027 share repurchase pace. PT remains $165, rating Neutral; analyst would turn more positive at a lower price if top-line growth accelerates. Starlink mobile entry flagged as ongoing risk.

bullets.title: DLR: Unusual options activity +317% on 1.4 GW EVGR LOI; stock -4.2% in market selloff
bullets.body: DLR saw 7,102 options contracts vs. 2,241 average (call/put ratio 9.87, bullish skew) following EVGR announcing a Letter of Intent with DLR for a 1.4 GW data center project. Despite bullish options positioning, DLR stock fell 4.2% to $177.19 in the broader market selloff.

bullets.title: META: Constructive post-Texas results; acquired AI coding startup Conductor
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes META viewed constructively after the blue Democratic sweep, as hyperscalers benefit from better FCF dynamics and tighter power-grid certainty. META also acquired AI coding startup Conductor. CDS spreads for hyperscalers (META, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL) tightened post-midterms.

bullets.title: PLTR, SHOP: Notable pre-market moves in flow data; SHOP -7.8% on earnings
bullets.body: SHOP fell -7.8% on earnings in Canadian markets. PLTR referenced in Hedgeye flow commentary as a focus name. Both names mentioned in JPM's Internet SMid earnings review webinar scheduled for 11/6 at 8:30 AM ET alongside RBLX, ETSY, and APP.

bullets.title: NET, TEAM, ANET: Piper Sandler post-earnings callbacks scheduled for 11/6
bullets.body: Piper Sandler hosting post-earnings webinars on Unity (11/5 at 1:30 PM ET) and Cloudflare, Atlassian, Okta, FIVN, FROG, SOUN callbacks on 11/6 at 8 AM ET with Jim Fish and Rob Owens. SHOP and ANET replays also available. No directional views disclosed in the invite.
